JudoScotland kyu grades

Which rules apply?

Scottish events use the IJF contest rules (the international rules), with a few national changes. The 2026 rules have applied since 21 February 2026, and small changes are made during the year.

Every event has an information pack. It always wins over this page, so read it before you enter.

Scores

IpponWins the contest straight away. Waza-ariHalf point. Two waza-ari make ippon. YukoSmaller score. Counted, but yuko never add up to a waza-ari.

Hold-downs (osae-komi):

20 secondsIppon 10 to 19 secondsWaza-ari 5 to 9 secondsYuko

Penalties

  • Shido is a minor penalty, for things like passivity or false attacks.
  • A third shido becomes Hansoku-make, and you lose the contest.
  • Some actions are direct Hansoku-make because they are dangerous, such as diving head-first into the mat, or high-risk armlocks while throwing.
  • Jewellery and hard objects are not allowed. Take everything off before you step on.

Kyu grade events

  • Low-grade events often ban strangles and armlocks. At the Scottish Student kyu tournament, novice to 5th kyu have no strangles or armlocks.
  • That event is open to players aged 16 and over who are 2nd kyu and below, novices included.
  • Other senior events for red and yellow belts can set their own restrictions. Check the information pack.

Scottish National Closed (2026)

Seniors14 or older, at least 3rd kyu (green). 4 minutes, unlimited golden score. Veterans30 or older, at least 4th kyu (orange). 3 minutes, or 2.5 minutes for M/F7 and above.

If either player is 60 or over, strangles are not allowed in that contest.

Referee calls

HajimeBegin MateWait or stop Osae-komiHold is on ToketaHold broken Sono-mamaFreeze, don't move YoshiCarry on (after sono-mama) Sore-madeEnd of the contest

Before you go

  • Valid JudoScotland membership. You show it at registration.
  • Check your weigh-in time. It is emailed and put on the JudoScotland website.
  • Short nails, hair tied back with nothing hard in it, no jewellery.
  • Clean judogi that fits the event's rules. Ask your coach if you're not sure.
  • Bow on and off the mat, and to your opponent.
Summary only. Rules change during the year. Check with your coach and the event information pack.
